title: Managing brands with creativity and humanity
speaker: Brent Smart

beats.say: Week four, with Brent Smart, former CMO of Telstra and IAG. Marketing is a battle for memory, and the biggest risk is taking no risk.

board.title: Managing brands with **creativity and humanity**
board.name: Brent Smart
board.org: Founder, B.Smart; formerly CMO of Telstra and IAG

beats.say: You're competing with how people spend their time. And categories look identical: bottled water is always an alpine stream.
Liquid Death broke every code and became the fastest-growing water brand in the world. Great ideas often sound stupid at first. That's the signal.
Creative work returns two and a half times the revenue growth and four times the profit of the average ad. Dull costs twenty and a half million extra.
He's proved it three times. Yellow Pages' treehouse used zero paid media. Cheerios rode out a backlash. NRMA's koalas went from thirty-sixth to fifth.
If it's not bold, it's dumb. Bad ideas are safe and comfortable. Good ones feel uncomfortable, and with no data, conviction does the work.
Telstra's reputation sat barely above the tax office. Asked to draw the brand, people drew a suit, the Monopoly man, a bully.
Only fifteen percent of buyers are in market now, ready for logic and offers. The other eighty-five percent need emotion, memories for later.
Don't just talk to the four hands that are up right now. Someone buying a phone in three years is worth reaching today.
Activation spikes, then drops when you stop. Brand building rises slowly. The benchmark is sixty percent brand. Telstra was at twenty, so he went to fifty first.
Be a magnet, not a mirror. Put a still from your ad, logo removed, beside three rivals. If nobody can tell which is yours, it's a mirror.
Telstra made twenty-six stop-motion ads, each an Australian animal in a real place, with forty-two local voices and handmade puppets. It won a Grand Prix.
The brand on one page: a connected future for everyone. Positioning, engineering possibility. The platform, wherever we go. Always crafted with a human hand.
The whistling ad used animation, no phones and metaphor. At launch, people hated it. But being noticed beats being liked, so he held his nerve.
Then people started copying the walk. Thirty million organic TikTok views, zero paid spend, and Telstra credited the people who made them.
Even the posters were handmade. People can tell made from generated, and read effort as care. Craft is a strategic choice.
Marketing ROI rose from six point one to ten point four in four years, on lower spend. Even performance marketing converted better, thanks to a stronger brand.
With AI, content is either slop or irreplaceably human. Telstra's AI Santa took eight hundred thousand calls. But you need an idea first.
So make the brand memorable, build future demand, and craft it with a human hand. Creativity thrives on kindness, so be kind. That's week four.
